Unit 1 of 10: Characteristics of Living Organisms

Key ideas

All living organisms show seven characteristics (memory aid MRS GREN):

  • Movement: an action by an organism or part of it causing a change of position or place.
  • Respiration: chemical reactions in cells that break down nutrient molecules and release energy for metabolism.
  • Sensitivity: the ability to detect and respond to changes in the internal or external environment.
  • Growth: a permanent increase in size and dry mass.
  • Reproduction: the processes that make more of the same kind of organism.
  • Excretion: removal of the waste products of metabolism and substances in excess of requirements.
  • Nutrition: taking in materials for energy, growth and development.

Worked examples

Example 1: a car moves and "uses fuel", but it does not grow or reproduce, so it is not alive.

Example 2: a plant shows movement when its leaves turn towards light.

Example 3: growth must be permanent and in dry mass; a sponge swelling with water is not growth.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) List the seven characteristics of living organisms. [4] (b) Define excretion. [2] (c) Define growth. [2] (d) Explain why a crystal growing in a solution is not living. [2]

Answers: (a) Movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion, nutrition (all seven B4; five or six B3; three or four B2). (b) Removal of the waste products of metabolism (B1) and substances in excess of requirements (B1). (c) A permanent increase in size (B1) and dry mass (B1). (d) It does not show all seven characteristics (B1), e.g. it does not respire or reproduce (B1).

Common mistakes

  1. Confusing excretion with egestion (removing faeces). 2. Defining respiration as breathing. 3. Missing "permanent" in growth. 4. Saying plants do not move. 5. Listing "breathing" as a characteristic.

Quick recall

  1. What does MRS GREN stand for? 2. Is egestion excretion? 3. Respiration releases what? 4. Sensitivity means? 5. Growth is an increase in what?

Answers: 1) Movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion, nutrition. 2) No. 3) Energy. 4) Detecting and responding to changes. 5) Size and dry mass.
